messages:
maria: ran an nsys trace on the kv-cache prefetch workflow this morning. weird pattern: when we use pageable allocations for prefetch chunks, H2D stall time spikes and overall tail latency climbs even though GPU kernels look identical. attaching timeline snippets below. :thinking:

maria: nsys summary (high level):
```
GPU active: 62%
PCIe H2D stalls: 24% of GPU time
cudaMemcpy (pageable): avg 650us/chunk (128KB)
cudaMemcpyAsync (pinned): avg 120us/chunk (128KB)
Host CPU busy: +1.3x with pinned allocations (copy threads scheduling)
```

maria: timeline (nsys/cuda kernel view):
```
[0.000] nvtx: kv_prefetch_start
[0.010] cudaMemcpy (pageable) -> long host wait -> GPU idle
[0.025] kernel: attention_forward (small bursts)
[0.040] cudaMemcpy (pageable) -> host pageable fault -> stall
[0.120] kernel: model_forward resumes
```

devon: interesting. did you also capture nvlink peercopy traces? which topology was used (p2p between GPUs or host fallback)?

maria: this run was single-GPU in a multi-GPU node so prefetch does H2D from host. p2p not used. I also ran a pinned variant where we pre-allocate a pinned slab and memcpyAsync into it before issuing H2D; that reduced the visible PCIe stall time to ~6% but shifted time to host copy threads and introduced queuing between prefetch tasks.

alex: that matches past behavior: pinned reduces driver/pageable faults but increases host-side CPU + PCIe DMA contention if too many concurrent transfers. how many concurrent prefetches did you issue?

maria: we trigger up to 8 concurrent prefetchs per request (heuristic tuned for throughput). with pageable, they serialize due to faults; with pinned they overlap and saturate the DMA engine -> bursts of small transfers create many short DMA descriptors. observed throughput variance: 9GB/s -> 11.5GB/s peak but with high jitter.

sam: can you paste the exact nsys command & config you used? want to reproduce locally.

maria: sure:
```
nsys profile -o kv_prefetch_trace --trace=cuda,nvtx,cudnn --sample=none --cpuctx-sampling=false \
  --capture-range=nvtx --nvtx-include=kv_prefetch_start,kv_prefetch_end -- python run_prefetch_bench.py --workers 8
```

maria: also grabbed perf counters: PCIe TLP retrain/gp stall events look low, so not physical link issue. more like driver-level queueing + small-transfer overhead.

devon: hypothesis: our batching heuristic issues many small prefetches (128KB). maybe combine into larger coalesced uploads for pinned path and fall back to serialized pageable uploads for small/low-latency cases. Also consider a prefetch token bucket to limit concurrent DMA submissions.

alex: +1. One more angle: kernel selection may affect KV cache access pattern — if we pick a variant that emits many tiny kernel launches, that interleaves poorly with host DMA bursts. Check timeline of tiny kernels vs memcpy windows.

maria: good call. timeline showed tiny attention kernels (~80us) scattered between memcpy windows. when pinned overlapped, the tiny kernels got starved intermittently, causing tail latency spikes.

sam: would measuring cudaEvent elapsed times around memcpyAsync + stream ordering help? and add NVTX around each prefetch op to correlate?

maria: already added NVTX spans per chunk in the trace; next step is to test two changes independently: (1) merge prefetch chunks into 512KB batches, (2) limit concurrent prefetches to 2-3 when pinned is used. planning an A/B run.

infra-bot: deploy reminder: perf env allocated on node gpu-prod-14 for 1h starting 1798805400 UTC.

devon: when you run A/B, please also capture perfetto + kernel occupancy view. perfetto will make it easier to see exact DMA engine overlap vs kernel execution.

maria: will do perfetto + p2p cross-check. if p2p path shows lower CPU overhead we might try promoting node-local peercopy for nodes with NVLink and do host fallback only when necessary.

alex: long-term we should adjust the runtime: prefer pinned slab pool for regular prefetches, but use an adaptive concurrency controller that measures per-token latency and backs off to pageable single-threaded fallback when tail > SLO. also consider batching heuristic that aligns with kernel batching windows to avoid interleaving.

maria: noted. I'll post the A/B results here after runs (~30m). thanks folks :thumbsup:

sam: thanks — if you need a quick script to coalesce chunks I have one, ping me. :eyes:
